chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, said:

A woman asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and she said: 'I was sitting (abstaining from prayer) due to my post-childbirth bleeding for twenty days, until they issued a verdict for me of eighteen days.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And why did they issue a verdict for you of eighteen days?' A man said: 'Due to the hadith which is reported from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying to Asma bint Umays when she experienced post-childbirth bleeding with Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Asma asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and eighteen days had already come to her, and had she asked him before that, he would have ordered her to perform the ritual bath and do what the one with inter-period bleeding does.'

key_terms.أَسْمَاءَ بِنْتِ عُمَيْس: Asma bint Umays, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on post-childbirth bleeding before eighteen days?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential principle that the eighteen-day period for post-childbirth bleeding (nifas) is a maximum limit rather than a fixed duration, establishing that prior to this, the rulings of istihaza (inter-period bleeding) apply. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the specific case of Asma bint Umays and the general rule, emphasizing that the Prophet’s instruction for her to perform ghusl and follow istihaza rules before the eighteenth day confirms the flexibility of the nifas period. This narration is pivotal in Shia fiqh for determining when a woman transitions from the state of nifas to that of a regular menstruating woman or one with istihaza.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, said,

‘A woman asked Abu Abdullahasws saying, ‘I was sitting (abstaining from Salaat) due to my post-childbirth bleeding (Nafsa’a), for twenty days, until I was issued with a verdict of eighteen days’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘And why were you issued with a verdict of eighteen days?’ So a man said, ‘Due to the Hadeeth which is reported from Rasool-Allahsaww saying to Asma Bint Umays, when she experienced post-childbirth bleeding (Nafsa’a) with Muhammad Bin Abu Bakr’.

So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Asma asked Rasool-Allahsaww and eighteen days had already come to her, and had she asked before that hesaww would have ordered her that she should wash and do what the one with the inter-period bleeding (Istihaaza) would do’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father in a marfu‘ the following:

“A woman once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I would, because of childbirth, wait for twenty days and they gave a fatwa to wait for eighteen days. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘Why did they give a fatwa for eighteen days?’ A man then said it is because of the Hadith from the Messenger of Allah who said to Asma’ bint ‘Umays for the birth of Muhammad ibn abu Bakr.

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Asma’ asked the Messenger of Allah after eighteen days. Had she asked before, the Messenger of Allah would ask her to take Ghusl (bath) and do what a Mustahadah is required to do.’”
